joint.outcome: theorem from standard axioms with no shared-scope hypotheses: consistent with every satisfiable law set

law.label: The bee's cell has least surface when its closing rhombi satisfy cos θ = 1/√3
law.statement_en: A hexagonal prism of side s and height h closed by three equal rhombi inclined at angle θ to the axis (the Maraldi–Koenig problem) has surface at least 6sh + (3√2/2)s², with equality exactly when cos θ = 1/√3. At that optimum each rhombus has the angle of the rhombic dodecahedron, cos = -1/3 (109° 28′), which is also Plateau's tetrahedral angle.

hypotheses.name: bee-cell-rhombic-closure#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: The cell is the ideal solid: regular hexagonal prism, three congruent rhombi, 0 < θ < π/2, enclosed volume independent of θ. Real comb cells deviate (wall thickness, rounded bases, Pirk et al. 2004's argument that the rhombic base is partly a thermal artefact); the theorem is about the model.

scope.basis: Euclidean geometry of the ideal cell; applies to the model, not to a measured comb
kernelChecked: Exact: 6sh + (3√2/2)s² ≤ beeCellArea s h θ, with equality iff √3 cos θ = 1 (beeCellArea_min).
At the optimum, rhombusCos (s√3) (s / sin θ) = -1/3 (beeCell_rhombus_angle).
Non-vacuity: θ = arccos(1/√3) lies in (0, π/2) (beeCellArea_min_witness).
assumed: Ideal solid: regular hexagonal prism closed by three congruent rhombi; 0 < θ < π/2.
